Application Data.NAME: Fresh Harvest Grocery Inc.
Application Data.CONTACT FOR INSPECTION: John Smith, Store Manager, Fresh Harvest Grocery Inc.
Application Data.DESCRIPTION OF OPERATIONS: Fresh Harvest Grocery Inc. operates as a full-service grocery store, offering a wide range of products including fresh produce, dairy, bakery items, and packaged goods. We provide home delivery services to enhance customer convenience. Our facility is equipped with state-of-the-art refrigeration to maintain product integrity and minimize spoilage. We prioritize food safety through stringent handling procedures and regular employee training. Additionally, we have implemented comprehensive security measures, including surveillance systems and cash handling protocols, to mitigate risks of theft and employee dishonesty. Our delivery operations are managed by a well-trained team to ensure safe transportation of goods.

Application Data.DESCRIPTION OF LOSSES: On 06/15/2022, a refrigeration unit failed, leading to spoilage of perishable goods valued at $20,000. The claim was submitted, and as of 08/01/2022, the status is resolved with reimbursement received. Additionally, on 09/10/2022, a delivery vehicle was involved in a minor accident, causing $10,000 in damages; this claim is currently open and under review. Total losses reported amount to $30,000.

Underwriting Guidelines:
Food & Grocery Stores face a variety of risks that must be carefully
evaluated during underwriting:
• Food spoilage, contamination, or fire: Perishable inventory is vulnerable to spoilage due
to refrigeration failure, power outages, or contamination from improper handling. Fire risks
arise from cooking equipment, electrical faults, and fuel storage (if applicable). For example, a
refrigeration compressor failure can lead to significant product loss and business interruption.
• Auto accidents in delivery operations: Stores offering home delivery or catering services
expose themselves to liability from vehicle accidents. Without proper fleet management, these
risks increase significantly.
• Crime, theft, or employee dishonesty: Grocery stores often handle large volumes of cash
and high-value inventory (e.g., alcohol, tobacco), making them targets for theft and internal
fraud. Robust security measures, including surveillance systems and employee screening, are
critical.
